summary: H.R. 8035 extends the expiration date for Title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 to October 20, 2027. It also extends transition procedures that keep existing surveillance orders, authorizations, and directives in effect until their individual expiration dates if Title VII authorities ever expire.

affected_groups.effect: Their communications may be acquired for foreign intelligence purposes under Title VII authorities.
affected_groups.group: Non-U.S. persons outside the United States

affected_groups.effect: Their communications may be incidentally acquired during foreign intelligence surveillance and subsequently searched under certain circumstances.

key_provisions: Extends Title VII authorities of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 through October 20, 2027.
Extends transition procedures so that active orders, authorizations, or directives continue until their specific expiration dates if Title VII expires.
Sets the effective date of the amendments to be either the date of enactment or April 19, 2026, whichever comes first.

summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 8035 extends the expiration date for Title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 to October 20, 2027. summary_detail.significance: The bill maintains current government authorities relating to foreign intelligence surveillance and electronic data collection targeting individuals outside the United States by moving the expiration date to October 20, 2027.
